title: Singular partitive demonstratives
summary: Choose tätä, tuota or sitä for a singular partitive reference.
objectives: Choose tätä, tuota or sitä for a singular partitive reference.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose tätä, tuota or sitä for a singular partitive reference.
A demonstrative points to something or refers back to it. The near, farther and already-mentioned cues remain visible before you answer. The noun and verb are supplied.
Learn tämä → tätä, tuo → tuota and se → sitä. Beside a partitive noun the demonstrative also takes partitive. It can also replace an already understood noun.
keyPoints: Use tätä for this nearby reference, tuota for that farther reference, and sitä for it or that already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.

steps: Use tätä for this nearby reference, tuota for that farther reference, and sitä for it or that already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Juon means “I drink” and works as the verb. juon comes from juoda: juo- + -n.
tätä means “this” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of tämä is tätä; learn this pronoun form directly.
kahvia means “coffee” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. This i-word keeps i: kahvi + a = kahvia. The back vowel a determines the ending.

examples.english: I am looking for that book.
steps: Use tätä for this nearby reference, tuota for that farther reference, and sitä for it or that already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
tuota means “that” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of tuo is tuota; learn this pronoun form directly.
kirjaa means “book” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep kirja and add -a: kirja + a = kirjaa.

examples.english: I am waiting for the bus.
steps: Use tätä for this nearby reference, tuota for that farther reference, and sitä for it or that already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Odotan means “I am waiting for” and works as the verb. odotan comes from odottaa: odota- + -n, with tt → t.
sitä means “it / that” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of se is sitä; learn this pronoun form directly.
bussia means “bus” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep bussi and add -a: bussi + a = bussia.

examples.english: I am looking for this car.
steps: Use tätä for this nearby reference, tuota for that farther reference, and sitä for it or that already mentioned, in the partitive pattern.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
tätä means “this” and works as the partitive demonstrative agreeing with the following noun. The standard written partitive form of tämä is tätä; learn this pronoun form directly.
autoa means “car” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Add -a to auto: autoa. The ending is selected from the word’s back vowels.

commonMistakes: Use the visible reference cue to choose between the three forms.
Do not leave the demonstrative in its dictionary form beside the partitive noun.

optionFeedback.tätä: tätä indicates one nearby reference. The visible cue instead requires tuota: one farther reference.
